title: Annotatio III §.VIII: Not deterred by Trent Sess. XIII cap. 4 Can. 2 — TRANSSUBSTANTIATIO defined
pass_a_gloss: By which Transsubstantiation is so guarded as is read in Session XIII chapter 4 Canon 2 p. 130 at the beginning: Since Christ our Redeemer said that what He offered under the species of bread was truly His body; therefore it has always been persuaded in the Church of God, and this holy synod now declares, that by consecration of bread and wine a Conversion is made of the whole substance of bread into the substance of our Lord’s body and of the whole substance of wine into the substance of His blood, which Conversion is conveniently and properly called by the holy Catholic (Roman) Church TRANSUBSTANTIATION.
pass_b_english: Trent Sess. XIII cap. 4 Can. 2 (p. 130): because Christ said what He offered under bread-species was truly His body, consecration converts the whole substance of bread into His body and of wine into His blood.
That conversion the holy Catholic (Roman) Church conveniently and properly calls TRANSUBSTANTIATION.
source_text: Quô Transsubstantiationi ita cautum legitur Sessione XIII. cap. 4. Can. 2. p. m. 130. initio: Quoniam Christus Redemptor noster, corpus suum, id quod sub specie panis offerebat, verè esse dixit; ideo persuasum semper in Ecclesia Dei fuit, idque nunc hæc sancta synodus declarat, per consecrationem panis & vini Conversionem fieri totius substantiæ panis in substantiam corporis Domini nostri & totius substantiæ vini in substantiam sanguinis ejus, quæ Conversio convenienter & propriè à sancta Catholica (Romana) Ecclesia TRANSSUBSTANTIATIO est appellata.

lemmas.gloss: a Conversion of the whole substance is made
